references.text: The prophecy about those who sleep in the dust and shall awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame, directly reflects Jesus' statement that all who are in the graves will hear his voice and come out.
God's promise to open the graves and bring the people out so that they may hear his voice and receive life is a clear parallel motif to the resurrection of the dead at Christ's voice.
The statement that the dead shall awake and sing connects with the theme of those in the graves hearing God's voice and being restored to life.
In the same chapter, Jesus foretells that the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God and live, which is the immediate context for verse 28.
The raising of Lazarus is a concrete fulfillment of the principle that those in the graves shall hear Jesus' voice and come out.
Jesus' own prophecy that he would rise on the third day confirms his authority to call the dead from the graves by his voice.
